tools.description:
Start 'fastsd', 'gimp' or 'all'. Idempotent. FastSD is launched and awaited. GIMP is opened by
the user via the 'GIMP + MCP' desktop shortcut: this returns what to ask them, or, with wait_s>0,
waits that long for GIMP's MCP port after you've asked.
tools.name: apps_start

tools.description: Which local services are running (FastSD, GIMP's MCP port), the inputs folder, the image backend.
tools.name: apps_status

tools.description: Stop 'fastsd' (frees ~4 GB RAM). GIMP is never closed by funkbox (unsaved work).
tools.name: apps_stop

tools.description:
Edit a COPY of a picture; the original is never touched. ops run in order, geometry first (crop, resize, rotate,
flip, remove_background, inpaint {mask, grow}, trim_even), then adjust {brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, ...}, filter {blur, sharpen,
...}, vignette, overlay {path, x, y, scale, blend, opacity, depth, shadow}, text {copy_id|text, ...}, border {px, color}.
Writes <out>/edits/<stem>-<name|n>.png, a sidecar that re-renders it, and a before/after sheet.
tools.name: image_edit

tools.description:
A licensed stock photo (Pexels, then Unsplash), saved to inputs/ with a credit record next to it.
STOCK FIRST: use this for almost every picture, and always for a picture with people. People pictures are never
generated: the tool answers NO MATCH instead (try other words). Pass fallback='fastsd_scene' only for a picture
without people that stock cannot supply; the result is then tagged as generated. Set people=true when the picture
shows a person even if the query does not say so. The credit line in the result must be shown wherever the photo
is used. Unsplash and Pixabay copies are kept for 24 hours and then removed; the next run removes them. Needs PEXELS_API_KEY or UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY in the environment; with neither set it answers NOT CONFIGURED
and sends nothing.
tools.name: image_find

tools.description:
Text-to-image with FastSD (SD-Turbo, OpenVINO on the iGPU); auto-starts FastSD. Aspect presets:
square 512x512, portrait 512x768, landscape 768x512, story 512x896, wide 896x512. n=2-8 returns variations
(seeds seed, seed+1, ... or random) as a contact sheet plus one file each in the inputs folder. seed -1 =
random (the seeds used are reported). steps 1 is best for SD-Turbo. COST OF SIZE CHANGES: the model is
compiled per image size (~2-3 min the first time at each size); this tool answers with a warning and does
nothing until you pass confirm_slow=true. PREFER 'square': SD-Turbo is trained at 512x512 and tall/wide sizes often duplicate the subject (two dogs stacked, a room on two floors); for 9:16 use square and let reel/stills cover-crop it (image_upscale first for sharper crops). Never request a product or text in the prompt. SD-Turbo output is
under the Stability AI Community License (free commercial use under US$1M annual revenue; Stability asks
commercial users to register). Not for pictures of people: use image_find (stock first, people never generated).
tools.name: image_generate

tools.description:
img2img: re-render an existing picture (a file in inputs/, out/ or the funkbox folder) following `prompt`.
strength 0.05 stays close to the original, 0.95 nearly ignores it. aspect None picks the preset closest to the
picture's shape (it is cover-cropped to that size). SD-Turbo needs steps*strength >= 1, so steps are raised
automatically and reported. A size not used since FastSD started needs confirm_slow=true (see image_generate).
SD-Turbo output is under the Stability AI Community License (free commercial use under US$1M annual revenue).
tools.name: image_restyle

tools.description:
Trace a picture (logo, emblem, flat art) into a vector SVG of a few flat colours, sharp at any size; use it as
an `svg` layer. ``palette`` (["#rrggbb", ...]) fixes the colours, else ``colors`` main colours are found.
``smooth`` 0 = straight segments, 1 = curves; ``tolerance`` (px) trades detail for fewer points; ``detail`` is the
longest side traced. Reports a fidelity score (poster_compare of the trace against the original) and shows
original | trace. Writes <out>/traces/<name>.svg and <name>.trace.png.

Lettering: ``lift_text`` takes text out of the artwork so live, exact text can go on top. Give the text colours
(["#1b224b", ...], or {"color": "#hex", "within": [x, y, w, h]} to look only in that part of the picture, as
fractions), or "auto". Letter-sized shapes of those colours (no side over ``max_letter`` of the picture) are
painted over from their surroundings and their lines come back as boxes (colour, box, angle, letters), also
written as <name>.text.json. With ``texts`` (the words of each found line, top to bottom) it also writes a starter
poster <name>.poster.json: the artwork as an svg layer plus a text layer per line in ``font``; poster_fit its
x/y/size (and skew_y/arc) against the original to line the words up.
tools.name: image_trace

tools.description:
2x upscale of an image (factor 2 only). Uses FastSD's upscaler when it works on this machine, otherwise
LANCZOS plus a mild unsharp mask; the result says which method ran. Saved next to the other inputs.
tools.name: image_upscale

tools.description: Return the source of shaders/<name>.frag.
tools.name: loop_get_shader

tools.description: GPU renderer/version, bundled shader names and the output folders.
tools.name: loop_gl_info

tools.description:
Everything you can use: v2 shaders with their @param ranges, post passes, blend modes,
layer types, plus the v1 presets/effects/palettes.
tools.name: loop_list

tools.description:
Render one frame of a recipe at loop position t (0..1). Recipe: {"settings"?, "palette"?
{"name","cycles"}, "layers": [...], "post"?, "text"?} - see loop_list. Give a named look instead of a recipe
to preview one of the looks. Fast; iterate here.

bevel.description: Light the masked shape from its edges so it reads as raised. Colour only; needs a mask.

font.description: A font, as the poster text uses.

size.description: Text height as a fraction of the frame height (poster range).

mask.description: What scales this layer's alpha: an image path (PNG with alpha), or typed text drawn by the poster text pipeline (the text is checked, so it is drawn exactly).

palette.description: The recipe palette: {"name": one of the palettes, "cycles": number}.

tools.name: loop_preview

tools.description:
Render a seamless loop (MP4 + PNG poster + JSON sidecar that fully reproduces it; GIF only if
gif=True, since it is ~10x slower than the mp4 on busy loops). Give a recipe, or a named look instead.
Limits: <=1080px per side, <=20 s, <=60 fps. Runs the loop check first and refuses a broken loop.

bevel.description: Light the masked shape from its edges so it reads as raised. Colour only; needs a mask.

font.description: A font, as the poster text uses.

size.description: Text height as a fraction of the frame height (poster range).

mask.description: What scales this layer's alpha: an image path (PNG with alpha), or typed text drawn by the poster text pipeline (the text is checked, so it is drawn exactly).

palette.description: The recipe palette: {"name": one of the palettes, "cycles": number}.

tools.name: loop_render

tools.description:
Grid of stills of one recipe (or named look) across seeds (e.g. "1-6" or "3,7,12"): the seed resamples every
shader's @param values, so this is how you pick a variation. Returns the PNG and its saved path.

bevel.description: Light the masked shape from its edges so it reads as raised. Colour only; needs a mask.

font.description: A font, as the poster text uses.

size.description: Text height as a fraction of the frame height (poster range).

mask.description: What scales this layer's alpha: an image path (PNG with alpha), or typed text drawn by the poster text pipeline (the text is checked, so it is drawn exactly).

palette.description: The recipe palette: {"name": one of the palettes, "cycles": number}.

tools.name: loop_sheet

tools.description:
One frame of a recipe (JSON object or .json path), a named look, or a shader (.frag path or GLSL source with
`vec4 effect(vec2 p)`) at time t (0..1 of the loop), as a PNG poster background in <out>/stills/.
``preset`` is the canvas size (square, story, landscape ...), not the look.

bevel.description: Light the masked shape from its edges so it reads as raised. Colour only; needs a mask.

font.description: A font, as the poster text uses.

size.description: Text height as a fraction of the frame height (poster range).

mask.description: What scales this layer's alpha: an image path (PNG with alpha), or typed text drawn by the poster text pipeline (the text is checked, so it is drawn exactly).

palette.description: The recipe palette: {"name": one of the palettes, "cycles": number}.

tools.name: loop_still

tools.description:
Compile a GLSL fragment shader (no #version line; define `vec4 effect(vec2 p)` or Shadertoy
`mainImage`), report errors in YOUR line numbers, run the seamless-loop check and return a
preview still at t=0.25. Saved to shaders/<name>.frag only if it compiles (and, with
check=True, loops). name: a-z 0-9 _ - up to 40 chars.
tools.name: loop_write_shader

tools.description:
Render a music score (JSON object or a .music.json path) to <out>/music/<name>.wav (48 kHz stereo) with real
sampled General MIDI instruments (GeneralUser GS, downloaded once; "soundfont": "builtin" needs nothing).
score = {bpm, meter, key, scale (major, minor, harmonic-minor, freygish, misheberach, dorian, ...), bars, swing,
reverb, tracks: [{name, program (GM 0..127), octave, velocity, pan, gain_db, notes: "^1/8 ^2 ^3 | [D3 F#3 A3]/2 r/4"},
{drums: true, pattern: {kick: "x...x...", snare: "....x...", hat: "x.x.x.x."}}]}. Notes are pitches (D4, Bb2),
scale degrees (^1..^7, ' up and , down an octave), chords [..], r rests, ~ holds; /4 quarter, /8 eighth, . dots,
! accent, ? soft. A reel can use the .music.json directly as audio.music (its beat grid follows the bpm).
tools.name: music_render

tools.description:
Render a poster's ``motion`` block as a video: <name>.mp4 (+ .gif), the last frame as <name>.png (the poster
itself: animations run towards the document's values), six frames on <name>-frames.png and
<name>.motion_audit.json (every frame's text). motion = {seconds, fps, enter: [{layer, effect: fade|rise|drop|
slide-left|slide-right|pop, at, dur}], tracks: {"layers.<id>.<prop>|dx|dy|scale": [[sec, value, ease?], ...]},
loop_shaders}. ``scale`` 0.5 renders a quick draft.
tools.name: poster_animate

tools.description:
How close is a render to a reference picture, and where does it differ? ``candidate`` is a picture path or a
poster (JSON object or .poster.json, rendered first); ``reference`` is a picture path. Returns scores 0..100
(overall, structure, colour, layout), the most different regions of a 4x4 grid, the reference's main colours with
the nearest candidate colour, and a sheet: candidate | reference | heat map. ``fit``: cover (crop) or stretch.
Writes <name>.compare.png and .compare.json to <out>/posters/. Use it to measure each fix, not to guess.
tools.name: poster_compare
poster_export_ora

tools.description:
Tune the numbers of a poster to match a reference picture: each key in ``params`` is a variations key
(layers.<id>.<prop>[.<index>...], e.g. "layers.band.points.2.1") with a step (0.01) or a [low, high] range.
Coordinate search on small previews, keeping only changes that raise poster_compare's overall score; text,
ids, files and path data are never changed. Writes <out>/posters/<name>.fit.poster.json and shows the result's
compare sheet. Use it after the design is right (shapes, glyphs, colours) to close the last few points.
``keep_inside`` (the specs of poster_fit_inside) rejects any candidate whose words leave their bar or plate, so
a fit to a reference with flaws cannot push the words out of the artwork.
tools.name: poster_fit

tools.description:
Size and place text layers so their words fit inside a part of the artwork (a bar, a plate, a label) with a
margin, as large as fits. Each spec: {"layer": id, "at": [x, y] (a point on that part, fractions of the canvas),
"band": half-thickness of a strip along the layer's skew_y angle (fraction of height; cuts a bar out of a bigger
shape of the same colour), "margin": 0.003, "tolerance": 60}. The region is the artwork colour around the point,
from the layers below the text. ``equal_size`` gives the layers the smallest of their sizes. Sets only size, x
and y (and align left, no wrap); the words never change. Writes <out>/posters/<name>.inside.poster.json.
tools.name: poster_fit_inside

tools.description: Canvas presets, layer types, blend modes, filters, effects, export formats and the edit operations.
tools.name: poster_presets

tools.description:
Render a small preview of a poster (JSON object or path to a .poster.json) and show it. Writes nothing.
Same layout and text as the full render, just fewer pixels. Look at it, fix, then poster_render.
tools.name: poster_preview

tools.description:
Render the poster at full size to <out>/posters/<name>.png (a project poster goes to the project's out/).
Also writes <name>.poster.json (the reproducible sidecar) and <name>.text_audit.json (what text was drawn and that it
equals its source). The poster's export list picks png/jpg/webp/ora/svg/pdf; ``formats`` overrides it
(svg and pdf are vector files with text as outlines, sharp at any size).
tools.name: poster_render

tools.description:
One poster in many sizes. ``sizes``: preset names (story, landscape, square, insta-portrait, twitter, a4-150dpi)
or {"name", "width", "height", "set": {"layers.<id>.<prop>": value}} with per-size fixes. Backgrounds stretch to
the new canvas; text, shapes, SVGs and products keep their proportions (a layer's "resize": fill|fit|top|bottom|
left|right|top-left|... chooses). fit_to="content" fits just the drawn foreground so wide or tall sizes use their
space. Every size gets its own exact-text audit; one that cannot be drawn is reported and the rest still render.
Writes <name>-<size>.png (+ formats such as svg/pdf) and <name>-sizes.png, a sheet.
tools.name: poster_sizes

tools.description:
Render up to 12 variants of one poster and return a labelled contact sheet. vary = {key: [values]} with keys
`seed`, `layers.<id>.<property...>`, `canvas.<k>`, `post.<n>.<k>`; several keys are zipped (same length).
Files <name>-<i>.png (+ sidecar) and <name>-sheet.png land in <out>/posters/.
tools.name: poster_variations

tools.description:
Approve the current draft copy and lock it as the project's copy.json. draft_sha256 must be the hash from
the LATEST project_propose_copy (a stale hash is rejected). The user is asked to approve the exact listing in their
client (a click you cannot make for them). Only if their client cannot show that prompt, pass
user_confirmed_in_chat=true: only set this after the user explicitly approved the exact listing in this
conversation. Never set it otherwise, and it never overrides a user's rejection.
tools.name: project_approve_copy

tools.description:
Build a FIRST DRAFT <project>.reel.json from the ingested assets and the APPROVED copy (it refuses an
unapproved or modified copy.json): hook first, body lines, a branded end card (lines named end_* plus url),
caption anchors that avoid the product, funk2 brand-colour filler when there are fewer than 4 visuals.
clip_share: fraction of shots that are video clips (default: follows the assets, e.g. mostly screen
recordings -> mostly clips). product_every: product in every Nth shot (0 = only on the end card).
formats: e.g. ["9x16", "16x9"] to render both from one edit. bpm: fixed beat grid for the cuts.
For a brief with exact timings, framing or push-ins, edit the returned JSON (or write the shot list) and
check it with reel_validate. Returns the reel JSON, the validate report and a storyboard.
tools.name: project_auto_reel

tools.description:
Derive the brand from the product cut-out and logo: primary (most saturated colour), secondary (darkest),
text colour (white or #111111, WCAG contrast >= 4.5) and fonts (the user's, else the bundled ones). Returns a
swatch image. Override any value with project_set_brand.
tools.name: project_brand

tools.description: Line-by-line difference between the pending draft and the approved copy.json.
tools.name: project_copy_diff

tools.description:
Classify and file what the user dropped: audio -> music/, video -> clips/, fonts and logos -> brand/, the
product photo -> product/ (with an alpha cut-out and a quality score), other images -> shots/. source defaults
to the inbox folder (files are moved); any other folder or file path the user names is only COPIED. Returns a
manifest and a contact sheet. If the product is ambiguous it returns candidates: ask the user, then call
project_set_product.
tools.name: project_ingest

tools.description: List projects with their status (new, ingested, branded, copy-drafted, copy-approved, reel-built, rendered).
tools.name: project_list

tools.description:
Start a project (a folder under projects/ with product/, brand/, shots/, clips/, music/). Then ask the user
to drop their files in the inbox folder (or tell you a folder path) and call project_ingest.
tools.name: project_new

tools.description:
Write a DRAFT of the ad copy: lines = {id: {"text": "...", "say": "optional spoken form"}} (id like hook,
body1, end_head, url; text <= 90 chars, written in the final case, drawn EXACTLY as typed). Nothing here can
reach the screen or the voice-over until the user approves it. The result is a numbered, exact listing:
show it to the user VERBATIM and ask for approval, then call project_approve_copy with the draft_sha256 it gives.
tools.name: project_propose_copy

tools.description:
Render the project's reel into projects/<project>/out/ (draft=true: 540 px wide, 24 fps, quick). The text
audit proves every drawn string equals the approved copy. Look at the poster, then render again with
draft=false. A reel with `formats` renders each one (<project>-<format>.mp4); format=<id> renders one.
tools.name: project_render

tools.description:
Override brand values: colours as #rrggbb; fonts as paths to .ttf/.otf inside the project or the bundled fonts/,
or as Google Fonts names ('Rubik:800', 'Secular One', 'Exo 2:700:italic'), fetched once and cached.
font_fallback draws any caption the main fonts have no glyphs for (default: bundled Rubik Bold, which covers
Latin, Hebrew and Cyrillic). Text a font cannot draw is an error naming the characters, never empty boxes.
tools.name: project_set_brand

tools.description:
Choose which image is the product (a file name from the ingest candidates, or a project-relative path such
as shots/x.jpg). Rebuilds product/product.png (real alpha kept, else a cut-out) and reports the cut-out quality.
tools.name: project_set_product

tools.description:
READ-ONLY. The copy deck: every copy ID with its exact on-screen text (and spoken text if set).
Use these IDs in shots. With project=<name> it shows the project's APPROVED copy.json and its lock status
(and, separately, any unapproved draft). There is no way to change the deck from here except project_propose_copy +
the user's approval.
tools.name: reel_copy_lines

tools.description:
Render the reel (or project=<name>) to <out>/<name>.mp4 (a project renders into its own out/ folder and
name defaults to the project name). Use draft=true first (540 px wide, 24fps, no depth model).
A reel with `formats` renders every format as <name>-<format>.mp4 (format=<id> renders just one).
Also writes <name>.text_audit.json proving every drawn string equals its copy entry.
tools.name: reel_render

tools.description:
One frame of a shot, t seconds into it (use shot_id 'end_card' for the end card). Takes a reel or
project=<name>; format=<id> for one of the reel's formats.
tools.name: reel_still

tools.description:
Contact sheet: one frame per shot (at its midpoint) plus the end card, with shot id, duration and
copy IDs printed below each frame. The fast way to iterate. Takes a reel or project=<name>; format=<id> shows
one of the reel's formats (e.g. 16x9).
tools.name: reel_storyboard

tools.description: Caption styles, end-card templates (with their copy slots), reveals, motions, transitions, anchors.
tools.name: reel_templates

tools.description:
A timeline page for a *.reel.json that the user and you both edit. action="open" starts it (if needed) and
returns the local URL to give the user: shots as blocks they drag to reorder, drag the edge to change length,
set in/out points, captions and voice lines, render a draft; saving validates first, keeps a .bak and logs the
edit. action="changes" returns that log in plain words (theirs and any made to the file outside the page), plus
the current shot order: read it before you change a reel the user has been editing. Your own edits to the
file show up on their page within seconds.
tools.name: reel_timeline

tools.description:
Check a reel (or project=<name>): schema, no literal text, copy IDs, files, caption fit, caption/product
collisions, timing, and for projects that copy.json is the approved, locked deck. Returns errors/warnings.
tools.name: reel_validate

tools.description:
Render several variants of one reel, one per position in ``vary`` (a JSON object, or its text), e.g.
{"shots.s1.source": ["clips/a.mp4", "clips/b.mp4"], "brand.palette": ["#f6f7f4,#0f7c6e", "#0f1216,#4fd1b9"]}.
All lists must be the same length (at most 12 variants). Every variant is validated before any render, then
rendered and text-audited against the approved copy into <out>/<name>-variants/. sheet=true also builds
contact_sheet.png, one numbered cell per variant's opening. Returns the manifest (variants.json).
tools.name: reel_variants

tools.description: Duration, size, frame rate, codec and whether a video file has audio.
tools.name: video_info

tools.description:
Find the cuts in a video (trailers, gameplay, screen recordings) and show one frame per shot with its times.
``threshold`` 0.05..0.95: lower finds more cuts. Writes <out>/video/<name>.scenes.json, which lists every shot
as a ready reel source {"video": ..., "trim": [start, end]}, and <name>.scenes.jpg. Pick shots from the sheet,
then use their trims in a reel.
tools.name: video_scenes

tools.description:
Burn subtitles into a copy of a video. ``cues`` = [{"start": 1.2, "end": 3.0, "text": "..."}] or ``srt`` =
a .srt/.vtt file. Drawn by funkbox's caption engine in a caption style (lower-third, red-box, bold-pop) with the
brand's fonts and colours (brand = {primary, secondary, text, font_caption, font_display}); Hebrew reads right
to left; text is never rewritten and a .text_audit.json proves each cue was drawn exactly.
tools.name: video_subtitles

tools.description:
Cut a piece of a video into a new file in <out>/video/ (the original is untouched, nothing is overwritten).
Times are seconds or [hh:]mm:ss. ``accurate`` (default) re-encodes for exact frames; false copies the
streams instantly from the nearest earlier keyframe.
tools.name: video_trim
